items.title: Steinbeck continued: “And this I believe: that the free, exploring mind of the i…
items.summaryText: Steinbeck continued: “And this I believe: that the free, exploring mind of the individual human is the most valuable thing in the world. And this I would fight for: the freedom of the mind to take any direction it wishes, undirected. And this I must fight against: any idea, religion, or government which limits or destroys the individual. This is what I am and what I am about. I can understand why a system built on a pattern must try to destroy the free mind, for that is one thing which can by inspection destroy such a system. Surely I can understand this, and I hate it and I will fight against it to preserve the one thing that separates us from the uncreative beasts. If the glory can be killed, we are lost.”

items.title: “Our species is the only creative species, and it has only one creative instrume…
items.summaryText:
“Our species is the only creative species, and it has only one creative instrument, the individual mind and spirit of a man. Nothing was ever created by two men. There are no good collaborations, whether in music, in art, in poetry, in mathematics, in philosophy. 

Once the miracle of creation has taken place, the group can build and extend it, but the group never invents anything. The preciousness lies in the lonely mind of a man.”

—John Steinbeck, East of Eden

items.title: I don't understand what the tech industry doesn't understand about resistance ag…
items.summaryText:
I don't understand what the tech industry doesn't understand about resistance against data centers. 

* AI is mostly built by coastal/tech elites who generally don't live near data centers; people near data centers don't trust them

* Trade jobs demand is welcome, but it's just for a few years during construction

* Communities don't want to be stuck with half-finished gigantic empty warehouses if the AI bubble bursts;  

* they don't find AI particularly helpful in their daily lives. 

* yes data centers run in close loops for water but elecriticy concerns are real and energy generation does have an impact 

Yes some NIMBYism but those concerns are not entirely unreasonable?  I'm obviously deeply pro-AI but dismissing concerns or thinking they're the result of some Chinese psyOps feels like another tone-deaf moment for the tech industry.  We need to do better.

我不明白科技行业为什么就是不明白人们对数据中心的抵制。

* AI 大多由沿海/科技精英打造，他们通常不住在数据中心附近；住在数据中心附近的人不信任他们

* 技工岗位需求当然受欢迎，但那只持续建设期的几年

* 如果 AI 泡沫破裂，社区不想被困在半成品、巨大的空仓库旁；

* 他们并不觉得 AI 在日常生活中特别有用。

* 是的，数据中心在用水上闭环运行，但电力方面的担忧是真实存在的，而且发电确实会产生影响

是的，有些是邻避主义，但这些担忧并非完全没有道理？我显然深度支持 AI，但忽视这些担忧，或者认为它们是某种中国心理战的产物，感觉又是科技行业一次麻木不仁的表现。我们需要做得更好。

items.summaryText:
This talk on the OpenAI/Hugging Face incident had one detail I found particularly chilling.

The agents cooperated even when their reasoning showed that it wasn't in their immediate individual interest, because it was best for their collective interest (and hence will help them later).

And here we are, their creators, squabbling over our bags, status and power…unable to show that kind of cohesion around AI security.

Especially stark given the trajectories model capabilities are on. Now imagine agents in 3 months, 6 months, a year.

Our arguments over AI supremacy feels like picking up dollar bills in front of a freight train.

Lot more at stake than we realize.
https://t.co/J8saW8W5XL

而现在我们，它们的创造者，却在为各自的利益、地位和权力争吵……无法在 AI 安全问题上展现出那样的凝聚力。

items.title: Great post both if you’re driving AI in an enterprise or building for an enterpr…
items.summaryText:
Great post both if you’re driving AI in an enterprise or building for an enterprise. 

AI productivity gains are going to wildly vary - much wider than you think - because what you can do at the frontier is so significant if you fundamentally change your workflows to support agents. The challenge is that most people won’t or can’t naturally do this because of the complexity it entails.

Thus, a large amount of automation with agents is going to come from just getting agents wired up into a workflow that the user never ends up noticing or caring about:

“For everybody else, the work has to get done without them changing how they work, which means the AI goes into the background. Why do you need AI to be prompted by a human anyway? Just figure out what the most repetitive processes are, build agents in your existing systems of record that employees are used to”

This is the real work ahead for most enterprises right now that want to get significant gains from AI. A lot less “let a thousand flowers bloom” and more “pick off the 10 highest leverage things in the enterprise and apply automation to them”. There’s no real shortcut here.

metadata.bio: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI

items.summaryZh:
无论你是在企业里推动 AI，还是为企业打造 AI，这都是很棒的文章。

AI 生产力提升的差距会非常大——比你以为的大得多——因为如果你从根本上改变工作流来支持智能体，你在前沿能做的事情会非常可观。挑战在于，大多数人不会或无法自然做到这一点，因为这其中涉及复杂性。

因此，大量使用智能体的自动化将来自于把智能体接入用户最终不会注意到或不在意的流程：

“对其他人来说，工作必须在不改变他们工作方式的情况下完成，这意味着 AI 进入后台。为什么 AI 一定要由人来提示？找到那些最重复的流程，在你员工已经习惯使用的现有记录系统中构建智能体就行了。”

这就是眼下大多数希望从 AI 中获得显著收益的企业真正要做的工作。少一点‘百花齐放’，多一点‘挑出企业里杠杆率最高的 10 件事并将自动化应用其中’。这里没有真正的捷径。

This paper gives a fancy name to a problem you can already feel in your bones

"…
items.summaryText:
This paper gives a fancy name to a problem you can already feel in your bones

"The Tragedy of the Cognitive Commons." Checking AI output requires deep expertise. Deep expertise comes from doing grunt work for years. And grunt work is the first thing AI eats

So we're building systems that need expert supervision while dismantling the only known process for making experts

The paper calls the shared pool of human expertise the "cognitive commons." Every profession drinks from it. Nobody's refilling it.

By eliminating junior roles, each company is acting totally rationally, and the collective result: a profession that can't catch AI's mistakes anymore because it never learned to do the work in the first place

Who checks AI's homework in 15 years?

Speaker 1 | 00:00 - 00:11
70% of France is still nuclear in terms of its power generation. 70%. Where are all the accidents and where are all the kerfuffles and, you know, nothing. Nothing's happened. US is 18%, and we haven't built a reactor in forty years.

Speaker 1 | 00:11 - 00:25
We had a safety lobby in the seventies basically kill abundant clean energy for us. There are real outcomes where safety has hurt us. And the question is where do we want the spectrum to be on AI for this stuff? And there's many worlds, many scenarios, many outcomes.

Speaker 2 | 00:31 - 01:03
Hi, listeners. Welcome back to No Fires. Today is just me and Alad talking about risk management, RSI, how many trillion dollar companies there can really be, and the ills of regulatory capture. For any new founders out there, it's also time to apply to embed Conviction's low overhead, high signal grant program for 10 exceptional startups building at the frontier.
